note: Captured a week BEFORE the deadline stated above. Committed now so git history is the evidence it predates the football, exactly as the round entries and the EFL tipster benchmark are. A week out is early: these are thinner markets than they will be on deadline day, and the numbers will move.

source.selfDescription: Real-time betting odds converted to goal, assist and clean sheet probabilities for Fantasy Premier League
source.derivation: bookmaker odds, converted — NOT a model of ours and not an official feed

whatThisIsNot: NOT our numbers. Nothing in the briefing or the app is rewritten from this. It is held against the register the same way the outside attack/defence ranking, the outside chip plan and the outside set-piece projection are.

NOT a minutes forecast. The player table says '(Assuming player starts)' in its own subtitle, which is the single most important caveat on the page: it assumes away precisely the uncertainty the briefing flags for Saka (eased back, achilles) and for the five European qualifiers carrying Thursday-Sunday rotation risk.

NOT a full player list. The player rows below are page 1 of 16, so a player's ABSENCE here means nothing at all. Gonzalo Garcia, added to the Fulham block on the same day, is not on page 1 and no inference is available from that.
gradeableAs: Per-fixture clean-sheet probabilities and per-player goal/assist/return probabilities, both resolvable against the GW1 result. The clean-sheet column is the more useful of the two because all 20 teams are present, so it can be scored as a calibration set rather than a top-N list.

verifiedAgainstOurRegister.method: Each row's opponent and venue diffed against the GW1 entry in the briefing's structured TEAMS array, mechanically rather than by eye.
verifiedAgainstOurRegister.observation: Full agreement on all 20 opponent-and-venue pairs, from a source built for a different purpose and with no shared upstream. That is the strongest independent confirmation the GW1 fixture list has had.

playersNote: Page 1 of 16, sorted by goal probability. The fixture label names the GAME, not the side, so it does not by itself say which team a player is on — Semenyo reads 'MCI-BOU' and this project's register has him joining Manchester City FROM Bournemouth for ~£64m, which the label cannot distinguish from the reverse.

opponentPointsConceded.whatItIs: A separate historical FPL signal on the same page, explicitly NOT bookmaker odds: average points conceded to opponents per match, plus the team's own average points.
opponentPointsConceded.completeness: Only two rows were visible in the screenshots. Recorded as partial rather than padded out.

observations: All 20 opponent-and-venue pairs agree with our register. Two documents built for different purposes from different upstreams matching on every row is the cheapest check available here and it passed outright.

Our four-band difficulty scale separates the ENDS and not the MIDDLE. Mean any-CS by our own label: easy 46.7% (range 34.4-60.3), mod 25.8% (16.9-31.9), hard 23.6% (19.8-28.3), vhard 11.8% (9.6-14.6). Easy and very hard are cleanly apart with no overlap; moderate and hard are 2.2 points apart on means and overlap almost completely. On this evidence the scale is really three bands wearing four labels, and that is a finding about our model rather than about theirs.

The one row where we differ by more than a quartile is NEWCASTLE AT HOME TO LIVERPOOL. We call it moderate; the market ranks it 17th of 20 for a clean sheet at 16.9%, below every fixture we call hard. If our rating is a read on Newcastle's defence it is a bet against this source.

Liverpool v Newcastle also has the LOWEST combined clean-sheet probability of the ten games (41.4 against 69.9 for Arsenal v Coventry), so the same fixture the market rates hardest to keep a clean sheet in is the one it expects most goals from. Those are the same statement seen twice, not two pieces of evidence.

Four Manchester United attackers sit in the top fourteen goal probabilities, all at HUL-MUN, alongside the second-best clean-sheet number in the league. The market's single strongest opinion this week is about Manchester United away at Hull.

Gyokeres has the second-highest goal probability of anyone on page 1. That does not settle the Arsenal penalty question, but it is now the second independent outside source this week leaning toward a striker over Saka, against our hedged line.

Saka carries the highest return probability of any Arsenal player here at 66.0% and the highest assist figure on the page but one. Read it next to the subtitle: '(Assuming player starts)'. The 11 August log has him eased back after a long World Cup with an achilles problem, so this source is at its least useful exactly where our own uncertainty is greatest.

Joao Pedro is at 57.7% to return against a Fulham side logged the same day as the oldest in the league with the fewest high turnovers, and he did not go to the World Cup. Three facts from three sources pointing one way is worth more than any one of them.
